title: Best Brochure Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a brochure designer: what the package should include, how to brief it, print-ready files, price factors and red flags.
intro: A brochure explains your business, product or event in more depth than a flyer, and is often handed out at meetings, events or in shops. It needs a clear order, good photos and a file your printer accepts. Brochures go wrong when the fold layout is misunderstood, text is not final, or the file is not set up for print. This guide helps you order one that prints correctly the first time.

faq.a: Common options are bi-fold, tri-fold and multi-page booklets. The right one depends on how much you need to say and how it will be handed out. Ask your printer for the exact template and share it with the designer.

faq.q: Do I need print and digital versions?
faq.a: Often both. A print file needs bleed and print color settings; a digital PDF for email or your website should be lighter and easy to read on screen.
Usually you. Some designers offer copywriting as an extra. Send final, proofread text to avoid extra revision rounds.

faq.q: Can the designer use stock photos?
faq.a: Yes, if licensed for commercial print use. Your own photos of your team, products or premises usually work better.

faq.q: Will I get the source file?
faq.a: Ask for it, so you can update prices, dates or details for future print runs.
